sql.description: The Truvio Commerce brand catalogue for SHOP1/ENU/EUR: 4 top groups x 3 subgroups (16 EcomGroups), 60 masters TCPROD0001..0060 with SKU TC-<CONCEPT>-<nnnn>, the Tier and Mode variant axes on 6 masters, BOUND to those masters through EcomVariantGroupProductRelation (the table that says which axes a product uses, and the one whose absence rendered every variant selector as an empty div while every other count was correct), with 36 combination rows, each with its own EcomPrices row, 1 BOM kit with 2 slots, 2 services, a 3-step quantity-tier ladder, one contract price scoped to customer number TC-100200, 4 product categories x 7 category fields with 180 populated values, a long description on every master (the PDP Overview band reads ProductLongDescription), and the tc_specs field display group over all 28 category fields, each named in the category-field reference form ProductCategory|<FieldCategoryId>|<FieldId> so the group actually resolves, which is what surface-swift's PDP spec table binds to. It also moves every currency row still carrying the placeholder rate 1 to 100. Every name is drawn from PIM/Commerce/CMS vocabulary (owner decision D-B); every key is TC*-prefixed and disjoint from sample-data's FIXT* and the feature families' PACK*.

The brand identities and their order history: the B2B account 100100 'Truvio Demo Account' (customer number TC-100200), the three personas 100101 buyer@ / 100102 csr@ / 100103 admin@ on the fictional truvio-demo domain, their memberships into the account and into the base-contract permission groups 1325 / 1292 / 1270, and 12 orders TCO-0001..TCO-0012 (20 lines) across the OrderFlowId 1 states New / Completed / Rejected. Runs after the deserialize rather than before host start because the orders FK the shop, currency and catalogue rows; the personas become first-class on the host restart the catalogue already requires.

sql.description: Product imagery: the 12 neutral concept tiles this layer ships under files/Images/TruvioCommerce/products/ become the default image of all 96 TCPROD rows, attached through EcomDetails (column set resolved from sys.columns, since the optional language/sorting/type columns differ across platform builds) and mirrored onto the legacy EcomProducts.ProductImage* columns where the build still has them. A missing EcomDetails table is a loud failure, never a skip: a demo that seeds no image and reports success is the failure this script exists to prevent.

The row-level B2B data the PLP and PDP need in order to say anything: a distinct one-sentence short description on all 60 masters, a five-step stock profile (healthy / low / zero-but-orderable / mid / deep) with expected-delivery dates and the matching per-location stock-unit rows, 96 REAL customer-group prices scoped to the buyer persona's own AccessUser group so a signed-in figure is visibly below list (marine fakes this: 22 price rows, zero with a user group), a three-step quantity ladder on ten masters rather than the one 1.1.x shipped, and five new contract prices on customer number TC-100200 beside the one the layer already had. Ends in a resolution guard that counts masters priced BELOW list for the persona, because a row count proves nothing about what the page shows.

What fills the product detail page, which the parity report measured at 84 characters of main text with four empty sections. A gallery of two to four images per master (the concept tile plus the photographic frame its top group is branded with, from the Distribution's own brand/brand-assets.manifest.json targets, plus a detail shot on two rows in five). The Manuals ASSET CATEGORY - one EcomDetailsGroup with extensions pdf, InheritanceType 3 and ControlType 0, the shape Swift's ProductMediaTable binds to when configured ImageAssets=["Manuals"] - carrying 120 document rows over the eight one-page PDFs this layer ships in files/Documents/TruvioCommerce/ and regenerates with tools/make-documents.py. 324 related-product rows in three groups (Related products, Accessories, Spare parts), with the kit story written BOTH ways so a member points back at its kit. And the remaining four category-field values per master, taking every specification table from three rows to seven. Ends in four resolution guards that assert what the page needs - two images, two documents, two relations, exactly seven specification values on every master - rather than what was inserted.

costHints.reservedKeyNote: The TC* family this layer owns, disjoint from sample-data's FIXT* / FIXTGRP* / FIXT-PRICE-* (base.contract.json idRules.reservedFixtureKeys) and from the feature families' PACK-<NAME>-* prefix. Recorded here until the next base release adds it to idRules.reservedFixtureKeys.
